summary: DHCP scope change disrupted DNS propagation across VLANs; Kerberos SSO failures on corporate Wi-Fi
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-12 (maintenance window), a DHCP scope edit was applied to the corp Wi-Fi VLAN (VLAN 220). After the change several corporate users reported SSO failures (kinit/kerberos) and inability to reach internal services while connected to corporate Wi-Fi. Symptoms also included inconsistent DNS resolution across VLANs and intermittent failure of hostname lookups for internal services.

Impact:
- ~35 users in US-west office experienced SSO failures and could not access internal web apps while on corp Wi-Fi between ~09:50 and 10:40 PDT.
- Developers using local VPN experienced some intermittent name resolution inconsistencies when their client machine received DHCP-derived DNS settings from the Wi-Fi adapter prior to establishing VPN.

Environment:
- Production corp Wi-Fi: VLAN 220 (office floor, us-west).
- DHCP server: net-dhcp-01 (managed via GitOps repo net-config), relay via edge-router-03.
- Auth stack: kerberos KDCs (kdc-1.redwood.internal), internal app hostname patterns (*.internal.redwood).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect a macOS or Linux laptop to corporate Wi-Fi (VLAN 220).
2) Obtain DHCP lease; inspect DHCP options (especially option 6 / DNS servers).
3) Attempt to kinit or SSO into an internal app (e.g., https://console.internal.redwood).
4) Observe failure to resolve KDC or internal hostnames; kinit fails with KDC lookup errors.

Observed logs and outputs:
- Client (macbook) on failing lease: "kinit: Cannot resolve KDC for realm REDWOOD.INTERNAL: Name or service not known"
- tcpdump on client: DNS queries for kdc-1.redwood.internal forwarded to 8.8.8.8; no answer for internal domains.
- /var/log/dhcpd on net-dhcp-01: "scope VLAN 220: updated, options: dns-server list replaced" (audit entry shows user 'netops-ops' modified scope at 2026-03-12T16:48Z)
- DHCP relay (edge-router-03) syslog: "dhcp-relay: relay packet for VLAN 220 policy applied: strip-option-6 true" (unexpected).

Initial hypothesis:
A recent scope edit inadvertently removed the internal DNS servers from DHCP option 6 for VLAN 220, or an ACL on the relay stripped option 6. Clients therefore fell back to public resolvers or received no resolver, breaking KDC lookup and SSO. VPN clients that obtained DNS from the Wi-Fi adapter before tunnel up inherited incorrect resolvers and saw intermittent failures.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Join corp Wi-Fi (VLAN 220).
2. Check DHCP lease: ipconfig getpacket en0 (mac) or dhclient -v (linux) to confirm option 6.
3. Attempt kinit for user@REDWOOD.INTERNAL.
4. Observe DNS queries; capture with tcpdump to see resolver IPs.
5. Confirm if client uses public DNS (8.8.8.8) for internal queries.
logs:
Client kinit error: 'kinit: Cannot resolve KDC for realm REDWOOD.INTERNAL: Name or service not known'
DHCP audit: 'user=netops-ops action=edit scope=VLAN220 old_options=[10.0.0.2,10.0.0.3] new_options=[8.8.8.8]'
Relay log: 'dhcp-relay: strip-option-6 applied for VLAN 220 due to legacy ACL entry 302'
investigation_notes: 10:05 PDT - Support ticket created by onsite engineer reporting multiple SSO failures.
10:12 PDT - Confirmed failing clients had DNS servers set to 8.8.8.8 (public) instead of internal resolvers via packet capture.
10:25 PDT - Reviewed DHCP audit trail on net-dhcp-01: scope edit at 16:48Z by netops-ops removed internal DNS list during a bulk update; change rolled out by GitOps PR merging net-config#442.

10:40 PDT - Checked DHCP relay (edge-router-03): found legacy ACL rule that strips option 6 for VLAN 220 when a 'strip-legacy-options' flag is enabled; this ACL was unintentionally re-enabled in the same maintenance window.
10:50 PDT - Re-applied correct option 6 on scope and disabled the relay ACL; restarted dhcp service on net-dhcp-01 (systemctl restart dhcpd).
11:05 PDT - Post-fix verification: packet captures show clients now receiving internal DNS servers; kinit and SSO tests passed for previously impacted users.
11:20 PDT - Noted root cause: manual scope edit + unintentional relay ACL toggle during maintenance. Change lacked rollback verification step in runbook.
comments: Asha Patel (10:15 PDT): 'Onsite reports SSO failures across multiple teams; marking P1. Gathering packet captures now.'
Liam Chen (10:28 PDT): 'Found DHCP audit entry showing scope change from netops-ops. Investigating relay ACLs.'
Priya Rao (10:45 PDT): 'After reapplying correct DNS list and restarting dhcpd, 3 test clients show internal resolution and SSO works. Monitoring for reoccurrence.'
Maya Ortiz (12:00 PDT): 'Please add a rollback/verification step to the DHCP runbook — we lost ~50m of productivity for several users.'
resolution:
Temporary fix: Rolled back DHCP scope change and restored internal DNS servers in option 6 for VLAN 220; disabled relay ACL that was stripping option 6. DHCP service restarted on net-dhcp-01 at 2026-03-12T18:50Z (UTC).

Root cause: Human error during maintenance/edit of DHCP scope combined with a legacy relay ACL that got re-enabled. The combination caused clients to receive public DNS servers or no resolver, breaking KDC lookups and SSO.

Permanent actions / follow-ups:
- Update DHCP change runbook to include post-change verification steps (DHCP options and end-to-end SSO smoke tests) (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2026-03-18).
- Add a CI check in net-config to prevent removal of internal DNS servers from corp VLAN scopes (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/net-config/pull/443).
- Review relay ACLs for legacy rules and add unit tests to prevent accidental toggles (owner: Network Security, due: 2026-03-20).
- Run a retrospective with netops and on-call support to adjust maintenance windows and communication channels.

Status: Resolved for now; monitoring for recurrence. Postmortem scheduled once monitoring confirms stability for 72 hours.
follow_up_tasks: Create runbook update PR (owner: Liam Chen).
Add GitOps CI guard to net-config to block removal of internal DNS in corp scopes.
Schedule relay ACL audit and remediation (owner: Network Security).
